newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Spot gold in Hong Kong ended up on Monday from New York's previous close on shortcovering from Europe after producer selling in the morning, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$321.60/322.10 an ounce compared to New York's close at US$321.00/60 on Friday.
"In the afternoon, European shortcovering drove gold up slightly," said one bank source, noting that market sentiment remained fairly nervous.
Australian producers drove down gold earlier, dealers said.
"The Australian dollar is slightly weaker and we saw a little bit of selling, forward selling to take advantage of the weaker currency," said another source.
Physical demand was said helping to boost gold prices, but not by substantial amounts.
"Unless we see a new range, physical buyers will be cautious," said one source.
The next resistance level was pegged at between $324 and $325, but dealers said that any gains were likely to be met by further producer sales, squashing any bullish sentiment.
Other traders said short positions on COMEX meant gold would likely go up if funds started to cover their positions, but that would be met by producer sales.
In the meantime, more selling was expected in U.S. markets. Local tael gold ended HK$2 down at HK$2,981.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil from its previous fix at -3.00.
